thread:
Mike Chen: heads up — after the continuous-batcher canary tweak (token_budget_target lowered) we saw a noticeable p99 jump in us-west-2, throughput down ~18%.
Sara V: can you paste the canary config that went out? link to the dashboard?
Mike Chen: short dashboard snapshot: p50 ~40ms -> 55ms, p95 160ms -> 300ms, p99 320ms -> 620ms in the 30m after rollout. throughput from 1.8k rps -> 1.5k rps for that pool.
AJ: what exactly changed in the heuristic? I remember we tuned pack_window and token budget.
Mike Chen: yep. Canary changed two things in cluster-config: lowered token_budget_target from 24 -> 12 and decreased pack_window_ms from 20 -> 10 for the continuous-batcher. snippet:
```
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: 12
  pack_window_ms: 10
  queue_policy: eager_fill
```
AJ: that would explain more microbatches/short batches. More single-request batches = kernel selection flips to the slower matmul path we fall back to for small shapes.
Jamie L: also check KV cache miss rate — if prefix cache miss increases we hit slow path to load KV which amplifies latency.
Mike Chen: ran a quick sampling of batch sizes in the window: results (last 15m): singletons 42%, size 2: 28%, 3-5: 20%, >8: 10%. Prior baseline was singletons ~12%.
Sara V: ouch. that aligns with the throughput drop. Any change in KV hit rate?
Mike Chen: KV hit rate jumped miss rate from 3% -> 11% on that pool after rollout. stack-trace samples show frequent fallback path in kv_store::sync_fetch.
AJ: sounds like two effects compounding: (1) token_budget_target too low causing many small batches and kernel warmup/inefficient kernel selection; (2) smaller batches increase per-request chance of missing prefix cache (less opportunity for prefix reuse) so KV misses amplify.
Jamie L: can we A/B revert the token_budget only and keep pack_window small? or just revert fully for canary?
Mike Chen: I'd prefer fast rollback and then a controlled A/B. This is a canary so rollback should be quick.
deploy-bot: @Mike Chen initiating rollback for canary group in us-west-2 — reverting continuous-batcher config to last stable (token_budget_target:24, pack_window_ms:20). Starting now.
infra-bot: rollback started. will post status updates.
Mike Chen: added a quick flamegraph snippet from perf samples (excerpt):
```
40% runtime: attention_glue::compute
18% runtime: matmul_small_batch_fallback
12% runtime: kv_store::sync_fetch
8% runtime: scheduler:enqueue_wait
```
AJ: matmul_small_batch_fallback at 18% is telling — small batch kernel path is expensive. We probably need a minimum batching threshold before selecting that kernel or avoid kernel-flip for transient small batches.
Jamie L: ops plan: (1) rollback canary (in progress), (2) add histogram sampling for batch sizes and KV hit/miss per model/version, (3) run a small A/B with token_budget_target=18 and pack_window_ms=15, (4) add short-circuit: if >30% of batches in last 1m are singletons, temporarily raise token_budget_target.
Sara V: agree. also add an alert for sudden KV miss rate >5% in a pool — that would catch this earlier.
Mike Chen: created ticket INF-6422 with the rollback + A/B plan and added relevant logs + flamegraph links.
deploy-bot: rollback completed for canary group in us-west-2 — configs restored to stable. Monitoring p99s now.
infra-bot: post-rollback metrics (first 5m): p99 back down to ~330ms, throughput recovering toward baseline. will continue to monitor 30m window.
AJ: can we also snapshot kernel-selection telemetry across the pool? want to correlate kernel flips with batch size distribution.
Mike Chen: yes. I'll add a one-off profiler job to collect kernel choice counters and KV hit histograms for the next 10m.
Jamie L: temporary mitigation: adjust scheduling to prefer coalescing small requests for same model shard for 100ms if pool load <75%. low risk and could reduce singleton spike.
Sara V: thanks all. postmortem notes: canary changes that reduce token budget can unintentionally increase singleton rates which both (a) push kernels into inefficient slow paths and (b) reduce prefix/KV reuse. We should add a checklist item for canaries that touch batching heuristics: run a microbatch-simulation before rollout.
Mike Chen: agreed. I'll attach simulation results to the ticket and schedule the A/B when metrics stabilize.
Jamie L: marking thread as actioned. follow-ups on INF-6422.
